extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editorial staff, contributors, and partners of The Texas Tribune
extracted.subtask_description: The Texas Tribune's public statement of newsroom ethics, sourcing, verification, conflicts rules, sponsorship/paid-content policies, and related editorial guidelines that govern how Tribune journalists produce and present reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and Attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Our reporting on all platforms will be truthful, transparent and respectful; our facts will be accurate, complete and fairly presented. Our analysis will represent our best independent judgment, not our preferences or those of our sources. There will be no hidden agendas in our endeavors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When mistakes occur, the Tribune will work quickly to fully address the error, correcting it within the story, detailing the error on the story page and adding it to a running list of Tribune corrections. If you find an error, email corrections@texastribune.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections policy
rubrics_metrics.description: When we make a mistake — and from time to time, we will — we will work quickly to fully address the error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections should be made within the story, detailed on the story page, and added to the running list of Tribune corrections; readers may report errors via corrections@texastribune.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution and Republishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribune journalists will not republish stories, images or other content from outside sources without permission and credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Tribune provides its news and information to Texas newspapers, news sites, radio and television stations to republish for free, subject to a few ground rules (see partnerships/reuse pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism, fabrication and misappropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism, fabrication and misappropriation of intellectual property are all grounds for immediate termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such conduct is a serious violation of Tribune policy and will result in disciplinary action up to immediate termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo, video and audio integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribune photo editors and video producers may improve the technical quality of photos and video or audio recordings, but may not alter the substance of that media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All photo illustrations, graphics or animations will be clearly labeled as such to avoid misleading readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: We will try our best to identify all of our sources, granting individuals anonymity only when the information is critical to the story, we are certain the source is reliable and there is no other way to obtain the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior editorial leaders must approve the use of anonymous sources. As much as possible, identify in reporting any bias known about sources. Anonymous sources should know that the reporter will share their identity with a senior editor, who will also keep that information confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: No misrepresentation of identity to sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Our journalists will never misrepresent themselves or mislead a source to get an interview or a story, and they will always identify themselves as journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters do not use hidden cameras or microphones, go undercover or pay for interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efforts to contact subjects and critics
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple efforts will be made to contact the primary subjects and sources of criticism in our stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should document attempts to reach subjects and ensure fair opportunity for comment when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decisions are made by journalists alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Tribune aggressively pursues stories it deems newsworthy; newsroom staff are not beholden to donors, sponsors or outside influence, and contributions do not entitle preferential treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of donor relationships in stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that reference or quote a Tribune donor or corporate sponsor who has contributed $1,000 or more will include a written disclosure that conveys when those stories are picked up by other news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All contributions are listed by year and by amount publicly; disclosures communicate potential overlap between sources and donors when relevant to republication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial roles in fundraising and promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Our fundraisers inform potential donors that their contributions do not entitle them to preferential treatment or relationships with newsroom staff, and in no way protect them from investigations or scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial employees may promote membership drives or be featured in marketing at their discretion; fundraisers and business staff solicit corporate support, not reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of sponsored content and editorial content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune accepts corporate sponsorships, underwriting and, within permissible limits, advertising that does not compromise its editorial integrity. All such support, including 'sponsor content,' must be clearly and obviously distinguished from editorial content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paid content will be clearly labeled as 'paid content' and visually differentiated so readers cannot confuse it with independent editorial content; sponsors play no role in editorial decisions; no political endorsements are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production and solicitation of sponsored content
rubrics_metrics.description: All corporate support will be solicited by the Tribune’s business staff, and no sponsored content will be produced by Texas Tribune employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business staff handle solicitation and sponsored messaging; editorial staff do not create sponsored pieces to protect independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of undermining sponsor/advertiser content
rubrics_metrics.description: Any sponsor or advertiser messages that contain false or unlawful content, or that the Tribune believes undermines its integrity, mission or brand, may be removed at the Tribune’s discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Tribune reserves the right to refuse or remove paid messages inconsistent with its standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funded-but-independent journalism labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes The Tribune seeks out content to be supported by funding from an entity — but this content is independently produced by our journalists and not approved or reviewed by the entity who helped to fund the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This content will include a note that it was supported by another organization to disclose the funding relationship while asserting editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest and vested interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists may not work on stories or projects in which they have a vested interest, financial or personal. They should avoid investment in companies or industries they regularly cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees must disclose and avoid assignments where personal or financial interests could reasonably call into question their impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary employment and freelance work
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists seeking secondary employment or freelance work to supplement their income must be cleared by an editor to ensure the work does not conflict with their responsibilities at the Tribune.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clearance process is intended to prevent conflicts with Tribune duties or coverage areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting honoraria and event roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial employees may moderate panels or speak at Tribune events underwritten by corporate sponsors, so long as their role is purely journalistic; any honoraria must be paid to the Tribune — not to the journalist — in the form of a tax-deductible donation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors do not determine panelists, subject matter or the line of questioning; outside speaking engagements must be managed to avoid conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts and travel payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribune employees, contractors and interns will not accept any gift with more than a nominal value from any company, individual or institution that could have an interest in the Tribune’s reporting. We always pay our own way when traveling for editorial or business purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This minimizes the appearance or reality of influence over reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on partisan political activity
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees, contractors and interns with any responsibility for reporting or editing the news will refrain from partisan political activity of any kind, including making political contributions or displaying partisan signage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule preserves newsroom impartiality and public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and fact-checking practices
rubrics_metrics.description: We investigate claims with skepticism; challenge conventional wisdom; consult data to verify claims by public officials; and confirm information with experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists are expected to verify and double-check information through interviews, research, data collection and data analysis. The Tribune may share relevant components of a story with a primary source or an outside expert to verify them. The newsroom constantly assesses whether information is verified and trustworthy and corrects errors transparently and promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to inclusion in newsroom and coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas Tribune seeks to ensure that its newsroom and its news coverage reflects Texas by including a wide range of perspectives from people of different backgrounds, ideologies and experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion guides hiring, sourcing and editorial choices to better represent state demographics and viewpoints.
